# PRD Index (Confirmed Scope Only)

*Last updated: 2026-06-25. Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx (signed-off requirements).*

This index defines which Product Requirement Documents (PRDs) are **authoritative and safe to implement** for the Zimmermann SFCC PWA frontend.

Anything not listed under "Confirmed" is either out of scope or not yet documented — do not infer or implement.

---

## ✅ CONFIRMED & SAFE TO IMPLEMENT

The following PRDs are based on confirmed, signed-off requirements. Agents may implement ONLY what is explicitly specified in these PRDs.

- **regional.md**
  Storefronts, URL prefixes, entry routing, mismatch detection, checkout ownership, currency/tax, Didomi consent defaults, marketing opt-in, GDPR (REG-001..067). Data migration, URL strategy, SEO and GEO have moved to **dataMigrationSeo.md**.

- **dataMigrationSeo.md**
  Magento→SFCC data migration, URL strategy & redirects, SEO (canonicals, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data), GEO routing (DMU-001..042). Split out of regional.md 2026-06-07.

- **analytics.md**
  GTM container, native SFCC data layer (single source of truth for downstream analytics/marketing tags), Didomi gating at tag layer, Optimizely audience attributes, Crazy Egg segmentation attributes. Optimizely & Crazy Egg are **not** in the GTM container (confirmed 09-06) — the PWA loads each as a separate front-end head tag (Optimizely: US-only, single snippet, page-head before render to avoid flicker; Crazy Egg: page-head from load); both still Didomi-gated (AAB-004/005)

- **homepage.md**
  Global header & icons, navigation (mega menu / hamburger), homepage content model (Contentful), Didomi consent notice, global footer, "Join Us" email capture, Inside Chat

- **search.md**
  Search platform (Einstein / Athos TBC), autocomplete with local currency, PLP merchandising, recommendations carousels (You May Also Like, Recently Viewed), open items (filters, Quick Add, colour swatches)

- **plp.md**
  Product Listing Page — product tiles, availability/buffer stock display, VIC exclusivity, model/item view toggle, search & autocomplete, recommendations, open items (filters, Quick Add, colour swatches)

- **pdp.md**
  Product Detail Page — page structure, product data (from Product API), product badges & tags, product states (Coming Soon/Back in Soon/Unavailable), pricing/tax/DDP-DDU display, availability/buffer stock, primary CTAs (slide-outs not modals), Find in Boutique (flyout panel with detailed spec), back-in-stock capture (stock alert slide-out), Find My Size/Measmerize, size guide, EU AGEC, content modules (Shop the Look, You May Also Like, Recently Viewed), product imagery/media, non-returnable indicator, VIC tag

- **cart.md**
  Mini-cart, cart page, cart persistence, wishlist, buffer stock system (delta feed every 15 min), inventory display, reservation rules, Find in Boutique (flyout panel), VIC exclusive products, back-in-stock notifications (via Emarsys)

- **checkout.md**
  Checkout entry → confirmation page (guest + registered + BOPIS flows), payments, Retail Rewards. Note: OOBO (RRC-019..029) is now **out of PWA scope** — strikethrough in the sheet; recommendation is to keep OOBO in Adyen.

- **orderManagement.md**
  Order creation and OMS export to MuleSoft → NewStore (OM-001..007, OM-036), BOPIS order export (OM-012..016), delivery-method/free-shipping-threshold export (OM-008..011), order tracking in My Account (OM-017..020, OM-035), inventory and buffer-stock display rules (OM-021..034). Created 2026-05-29.

- **returns.md**
  Non-returnable product rules, returns initiation (Narvar domestic / Global-e international), Returns page in My Account, cancellation & order status display, fraud-flagged order behaviour

- **account.md**
  Account architecture (global account / separate bags), registration, login, My Account sections (orders, returns, saved cards, wishlist, loyalty, communication preferences), VIC access, GDPR

- **giftcards.md**
  Gift card & credit note PDP, mini-cart, cart (digital/physical), checkout flows by cart combination, GiveX redemption, payment combinations, Global-e restrictions, balance check in My Account

- **promotions.md**
  Promotions engine — coupon codes, stacking rules, promotion set-ups (PRC-20..32). Pricing, currency and Global-e handoff have moved to **pricing-currency-globale.md**.

- **pricing-currency-globale.md**
  Price feeds & pricebooks (AP21 base RRP + fixed Global-e pricelists), price display & tax, sale/markdown pricing, multi-currency & FX (nightly job), VIC & customer group pricing, Global-e pricing & cart handoff (PRC-01..19, 33..55). Split out of promotions.md 2026-06-07.

- **delivery.md**

## CLAIM 1 — `productSubTotal` excludes order-level adjustments

**Verdict: CONFIRMED.**

The consequence first: if you read `productSubTotal` as "what the customer's basket of goods costs after every discount," you will under-report the discount and over-report what's left to pay — for the claim's own numbers, you'd think the customer still owes 1000 when they actually owe 800. That's the exact bug shape this field name invites.

Mechanism, from source — `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts` (package version `5.2.0`, matching the pin in `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/package.json:44`, so this is genuinely what this project resolves, not a stale copy):

- `Basket.productSubTotal`, `index.esm.d.ts:7040`: *"The total price of all products including item-level adjustments, **but not including order-level adjustments** or shipping charges."*
- `Basket.productTotal`, `index.esm.d.ts:7042`: *"The total price of all products including adjustments, but not including shipping charges."* — the sibling `Shipment` type's equivalent field (`index.esm.d.ts:6667`) spells the same fact out unambiguously: *"including item-level adjustments **and prorated order-level adjustments**."*
- `Basket.orderTotal`, `index.esm.d.ts:7034`: *"The total price, including products, shipping and tax."*
- `Basket.orderPriceAdjustments`, `index.esm.d.ts:7032`: *"The order-level price adjustments"* — a sibling field, not something `productSubTotal` folds in.

I checked this held for `Order` (post-checkout) too, since `order-summary/index.tsx`'s own comment says it renders both baskets and orders: `Order.productSubTotal`/`productTotal`/`orderTotal` at `index.esm.d.ts:33414-33477` carry the identical semantics (one field's doc comment has a stray "in the shipment" copy-paste artifact from the `Shipment` type, but the "not including order-level adjustments" clause is intact and unchanged).

So, applying this to the claim's own numbers — one line at `price: 1000`, order-level promo `-200`:
- `productSubTotal` = **1000** (item-level only; order-level excluded — matches the claim exactly)
- `productTotal` = **800** (1000, then the −200 order-level adjustment prorated in)
- `orderTotal` = `productTotal` + `shippingTotal` + `taxTotal` = 800 + shipping + tax (not fully computable without those two numbers, but the relationship is unambiguous)

**What I could not settle:** I found no committed fixture/mock JSON anywhere in the repo (searched all `.json`/`.ts`/`.tsx`/`.js` outside `node_modules` for `productSubTotal`/`orderPriceAdjustments`) showing a real captured basket response with these three numbers side by side — the only matches were the SDK's own type declarations and `order-summary/index.tsx` itself. So this is settled from the SDK's embedded API contract, not a live-captured example. A live sandbox basket with a real order-level promotion applied would be the only strictly stronger source than this — but the type doc is the API provider's own contract, not a guess, so I don't think that gap weakens the verdict.

## CLAIM 2 — the PRD requirement and the discount-line-format question

Two separate sub-claims bundled together here. Treating them separately, because they land differently.

### 2a. The visibility requirement text and the "cart-only discounts" distinction

**Verdict: PLAUSIBLE, narrower than stated — the text is CONFIRMED, the "confirmed requirement ID" framing is not.**

`.docs/prd/pricing-currency-globale.md:63` reads verbatim: *"Customer-group-specific catalogue pricing — visible on PLP, PDP, mini-bag, cart, checkout, recommended tiles, wishlist (**not cart-only discounts**). Discounts do not apply to products already on sale or to gift cards."* That's an exact match for the claim's seven surfaces and the "cart-only discounts" distinction — **CONFIRMED** as text.

Where the claim overreaches: it asks me to "quote the requirement ID." I can't, honestly, and here's why that's not just me not looking hard enough (scope: I read the entire file, `.docs/prd/pricing-currency-globale.md`, end to end). The sentence at line 63 carries **no inline ID** — unusual, since almost every other bullet in this same document tags itself (`PRC-09`, `PRC-18`, etc.). The section header at line 61 claims a range, `## 5. VIC & Customer Group Pricing (PRC-17 – PRC-19)`. Of that range, `PRC-18` and `PRC-19` are both explicitly spoken for by two *later, different* sentences (lines 73–74: the no-stacking-on-sale rule, and the BM priority-rules config). That leaves `PRC-17` as the only number in the header's range not yet claimed by anything in section 5 — except the document's own Section 7 Open Items (line 96) explicitly assigns `PRC-17` to something else entirely: *"Platinum VIC permanent discount rate — TBC (PRC-17)"* — a fact about one table row, not the visibility statement. The intro note at line 9 repeats this same attribution. So the one candidate ID is contradicted by the document's own cross-reference, not merely absent. What's actually true: **this requirement's text exists and is unambiguous; its requirement ID is not resolvable from this document alone** — that would need the source workbook (*"Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheet 'Price, Currency, Promo'"*, cited at line 5) to confirm whether line 63 is really `PRC-17` (and the Section 7 note is the thing that's slightly mis-scoped) or whether it's an uncredited requirement with no dedicated number at all.

Same reasoning applies to "confirmed requirement" — no sentence-level `(confirmed)` tag exists at line 63, unlike its neighbours. It's presumably confirmed only by the document's general framing (line 9: most PRC items are confirmed, open ones are enumerated in Section 7, and this one isn't in that enumeration) — an inference, not a direct read.

**Does it constrain how a customer-group discount should be surfaced in the cart?** Yes, but not the way the framing implies. It requires the *item's own displayed price* to already be the discounted catalogue price in the cart (same as PLP/PDP/etc.) — it is explicitly **not** a "cart-only discount" pattern. Read the other direction, this is actually an argument *against* modelling a Gold-VIC discount as a distinct "discount applied" line the way `order-summary/index.tsx` currently renders `orderPriceAdjustments` (`{adjustment.itemText} Applied`, line ~248) — that pattern is for the *other* class of discount (promo codes, order-level promotions), the one this requirement is explicitly drawing a contrast against. Worth flagging: if VIC pricing is genuinely catalogue-level, it likely never shows up as a distinct `orderPriceAdjustments` entry in the SCAPI response at all — it's just baked into each item's own `price` — which means Claim 1's fields (`productSubTotal`/`productTotal`) may not even be the right place to look for it.

### 2b. Does any PRD spec the FORMAT of an order-summary discount line?

**Verdict: CONFIRMED that one exists — UNSUPPORTED that it covers customer-group discounts.**

Found: `.docs/prd/checkout.md:211`, under `## 12. Retail Rewards (PAY-027 – PAY-040)`: *"Displayed as a separate named line item in the order summary (e.g. \"DISCOUNT | GOLD VIP - 10% OFF\"), showing the amount deducted from subtotal (**PAY-028**)."* That's exact and reproducible — a real format spec (named line, `DISCOUNT | <segment> - <pct>% OFF` example, amount off subtotal) with a real ID.

But: this is scoped to **Retail Rewards**, and the same document is explicit two bullets later, `checkout.md:215` (PAY-032): *"Retail Rewards are a **voucher payment method, not a discount**."* So PAY-028 is a format spec for a payment mechanism that the PRD itself says isn't a discount — not a mandate for how a customer-group catalogue discount (Section 5 above) or a coupon/promo (`promotions.md` PRC-27/29, which specify *where* promotions show, not *how* they're worded) should be labelled. Search scope for "no broader format spec exists": grepped every file in `.docs/prd/*.md` for `discount line|order summary|promotion name|itemText|line item.*(discount|promo)|% ?off|named line`, and read `cart.md`, `checkout.md`, `promotions.md`, `pricing-currency-globale.md`, `giftcards.md` in full or by matched section — nothing else specifies a discount-line text format. What's actually true: no PRD-mandated format exists for a customer-group or coupon discount line; PAY-028 is the nearest analog and doesn't reach that far.

## CLAIM 3 — does the new test/story pair render the base `item-price`?

Split exactly as asked.

**The import itself — CONFIRMED, but not new to this commit.** `overrides/app/components/order-summary/index.tsx:29` at `1a32bc94`: `import CartItemVariantPrice from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-price'`. Confirmed this predates the commit — `git show 1a32bc94 -- overrides/app/components/order-summary/index.tsx` shows the only diff in that file is 13 lines around the coupon-removal guard (lines ~386-410); line 29 is untouched. `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-price.tsx` genuinely exists as a real override at this commit (confirmed via `git show 1a32bc94:overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-price.tsx`) and materially differs from the base (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-price.jsx`) — it adds order-discount price handling (`priceAfterOrderDiscount`), a sale-price crossed-out treatment, and a `ZimmProductPrice` atom the base doesn't have. So "base vs. override" is not a cosmetic distinction here — the two would render visibly different output if either mounted.

**Vitest — CONFIRMED it would resolve to base if rendered; UNSUPPORTED that this test file actually renders it.** `vitest.config.ts:40-71`'s `resolve.alias` has entries only for `~`, `app`, and three `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react*` bare specifiers — nothing for `@salesforce/retail-react-app`. I ran the suite for real, in the isolated worktree: `npx vitest run overrides/app/components/order-summary/index.test.tsx` at `1a32bc94` → **7 passed**, with `item-price`, `item-image`, and `item-variant` (index) left deliberately unmocked (only `../icons`, `promo-code`, `link`, `item-name`, `item-attributes`, `promo-popover` are mocked, per the file's own header comment). I also confirmed why that's safe: `require.resolve('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-price.jsx')` finds the real base file on disk (Node's default resolver just doesn't try `.jsx` without the explicit extension — there's no `exports` map blocking it, confirmed via `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/package.json`). So the mechanism is real. But it doesn't fire here: `CartItemVariantPrice` only renders inside `CartItems`, itself gated by `{showCartItems && <CartItems basket={basket} />}` in `index.tsx`, and `showCartItems` defaults to `false`. All 7 tests call the file's own `renderOrderSummary` helper (`index.test.tsx:90-97`), which never passes `showCartItems`. **What's actually true: this test file renders neither the base nor the override `item-price` — `CartItems` never mounts at all.**

**Storybook — CONFIRMED it would resolve to base if rendered; UNSUPPORTED that this stories file actually renders it.** `.storybook/main.js:29`: `webpackConfig.resolve.alias['@salesforce/retail-react-app'] = path.resolve(__dirname, '../node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app')` — an explicit, deliberate alias to `node_modules`. I verified this empirically (not just by reading the config text) by running that exact alias map through `enhanced-resolve` — the real resolver webpack uses — against the same import path: it resolves to `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant/item-price.jsx`, confirmed base, never `overrides/`. But again, it doesn't matter here: all four story exports (`Default`, `ShippingPromotionOnLaterShipment`, `FreeShipping`, `ShippingTotalUnavailable`, `index.stories.tsx`) pass only a `basket` arg — none set `showCartItems`, and the shared `meta` object sets no default for it either. Same gate, same result: `CartItems` never mounts.

**Does it matter for what these files assert? No.** Both files say so themselves — the test file's header comment scopes it to exactly two CodeRabbit findings (shipping-promotion aggregation across shipments, and `shippingTotal`'s Free/formatted/TBD branching); the stories file's own comments track the same two things. Neither makes any assertion about item pricing, sale-price display, or `ItemPrice` at all. So the claim's premise is real as a general resolution fact, but false as applied to these two files — and even in the counterfactual where it *did* render base instead of override, it would be irrelevant to what either file checks.

**What I could not verify:** I did not run a full Storybook webpack build (that's a materially heavier op — full-tree indexing across every `*.stories.tsx` glob match — for a question the `enhanced-resolve` run plus the complete, already-quoted source of both files already answers deterministically; there's no runtime branching a live build could surface that source-reading doesn't already show). If anyone wants that last mile closed empirically rather than by resolver simulation, running `Storybook`'s dev server and inspecting the rendered DOM for `Default`/etc. would confirm zero DOM nodes attributable to either `item-price` variant — but I'd expect it to just reconfirm this.
